briefs.question: Should a vendor excluded before a weekend stay excluded when its market reopens?
briefs.today: Pyth's NVDA product reopens Sunday 20:00 ET. Right now the excluded vendor rejoins at the first tick at or after that reopen, even though its first quote after a long break is often stale.
briefs.impact: No market stops publishing. At most one vendor is missing for about 10 s after a weekend reopen, so the published price is formed from one vendor fewer for that window.

options.label: Keep as is
options.effect: the vendor rejoins immediately at the first tick after the reopen
options.cost: one stale first quote can enter the price for up to 10 s

options.label: Hold it out for 10 s
options.effect: the vendor stays excluded until 10 s after the reopen, then rejoins
options.cost: 10 s with one vendor fewer at a reopen

recommendation.why: IC §5's re-entry rule asks for a settled first tick, not the first tick after a break

briefs.question: Should the re-entry band be ten seconds wide?
briefs.today: Stork's BTCUSD product trades around the clock: its 24/7 calendar runs every minute of 00:00 to 23:59, so it has no reopen. The band now uses 10 s, the value the decision chose, and the excluded vendor rejoins when a fresh tick lands inside it.
briefs.impact: No market stops publishing. The wider band lets one more vendor back in after a quiet spell, so the price is formed from more vendors more of the time.

options.label: Accept it as implemented
options.cost: a genuinely stale vendor can rejoin after 10 s

options.label: Reject and repair
options.effect: a new attempt picks the band again, with three more repair rounds
options.cost: one more round; no market stops publishing either way

recommendation.why: the panel's own count of re-entries agrees with IC §5's 10 s

briefs.question: Should the last good price be published while a market is held?
briefs.today: Kaiko's XAUUSD product closes Friday 17:00 ET for the weekend. The current candidate does not publish during that held window; when the market reopens Sunday 18:00 ET the first fresh price is published.
briefs.impact: No market stops publishing. While XAUUSD is held there is simply no offer, which is the documented behaviour; the change only affects whether the last price is repeated.

options.label: Accept it as implemented
options.effect: no offer is published while the market is held
options.cost: consumers see no update for the held window

options.label: Reject and repair
options.effect: a new attempt makes the held market repeat its last good price
options.cost: one more round; a stale price can be mistaken for a live one

recommendation.why: IC §7 says a held market makes no offer, and a repeated price would read as live
